To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

interference-free TP-LIF measurements of hydrogen atoms can be obtained using either nanosecond or picosecond lasers, and the optimum excitation pulse width is dependent on the H atom concentration and the concentrations of photolytic precursers.

the interference-free signal of H atom TP-LIF is significantly larger for picosecond than for nanosecond excitation, and the optimal excitation pulsewidth for interference-free H-atom detection depends on the flame temperature, the flame H atom and photolytic precursor concentrations, and the laser excitation path length within the flames.

interference-free two-photonic laser-induced fluorescence of atomic hydrogen can be obtained with either nanosecond or picosecond pulsed excitation, but the optimal pulse width depends on the relative hydrogen atom and photolytic precursor concentrations, the flame temperature and the laser pathlength.
